description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the “Ratio” (x-axis) and the “minFDE₂₀ (–)” metric (y-axis) for five different trajectory prediction methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, LoRA 16, LoRA 64, and an unlabeled green line (likely another variant or baseline). The x-axis, labeled “Ratio,” spans from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of context or training data used. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (–),” ranges from 0.8 to 1.3 in linear increments of 0.1, indicating the minimum final displacement error over 20 predictions — lower values denote better performance. The “TrajICL” method (blue line with circle markers, solid line) remains relatively flat, starting at approximately 0.90 at Ratio=0.0 and ending near 0.86 at Ratio=1.0. “Head Tuning” (orange line with circle markers, solid line) starts high at ~1.35 and steadily declines to ~1.08. “LoRA 16” (red line with circle markers, solid line) begins at ~1.22 and decreases to ~0.93. “LoRA 64” (purple line with circle markers, solid line) starts at ~1.21 and drops to ~0.93. The unlabeled green line (solid line with circle markers) begins at ~1.12, declines to ~0.83 at Ratio=0.8, and then drops sharply to ~0.75 at Ratio=1.0. All lines show a general downward trend, suggesting improved performance with higher ratios, though the rate and extent of improvement vary by method.
